title: Execute Glm assignments with native identity, team operations and accountable receipts
goal: Make the Glm execution environment a conforming team participant through its real native runtime and accounting contract.
scope: Implement ExecutionBackend(Glm) and explicit native discovery/readiness. Identify the actual local execution protocol and supported models/efforts/capabilities, preserving agent identity and authentication in that native environment.

Map start/cancel/events/receipt, native session/profile settings, structured role response and scoped TeamOperation transport into the shared admitted execution consumer. Native success/output never becomes a kernel verdict or new authority.

Normalize total input, cache-read/write, output and optional reasoning counts with Complete/Partial/Unknown coverage, preserving cumulative/resumed-counter attribution. Report unsupported controls and typed failures without guessing missing family/settings.

Exercise direct and IsolatedCopy permission/context guarantees and recovery through actual host contract fixtures, with an explicit real-provider invocation recipe for separately authorized verification.
acceptance: A Glm protocol fixture runs through Registry/Gatekeeper/Dispatcher, posts a scoped team operation, submits role output and settles a traceable receipt; unsupported/missing native dependencies are excluded before inference.
Malformed output, mismatched invocation/session, foreign grant, partial/cache usage and uncertain cancellation cannot corrupt resources, leak hidden context or accept a result.

Glm and a materially different backend run the shared contract through actual consumers. Fixture and real native evidence remain distinct, with native identities/authentication and unknown metadata preserved.

Scoped cancellation/reattachment fixtures distinguish parent exit or stream loss from validated cessation, retain holds/cost until their independent conditions and do not duplicate execution. Native choices are explicit supported offerings; experiment parameters never invent model/effort support or bypass §3.9/R-19/R-20.
context: Authority: ymp-docs/self-organizing-team-domain-model.md, sections 3.1/3.4/3.7, 5.1 (ReadinessProbe), 5.7 (ExecutionBackend), A5/A13 and R-2/R-3/R-8/R-9/R-10. Use the approved model with 811a872 semantics and the greenfield baseline in 0c61ff1 and §5.8 for experimental strategy boundaries. Other documents and existing names explain implementation facts only.

Greenfield: create this behavior in the new implementation. Paths below are PROPOSED target modules under the layout owned by W1-0001; only completed prerequisite tasks supply implementation. Prior source, APIs, fixtures and delivery claims are not a baseline.

Create proposed crates/ymp-runtime/src/backends/glm.rs and new protocol fixtures. W1-0017 supplies the execution contract, W3-0001 team transport and W4-0001 workspace enforcement. Build the full native Glm adapter, not a provider-kind alias.

Resolve the actual supported native environment/protocol from installed/official information. Shared transport is appropriate only if that environment supports it; Glm identity cannot be replaced with Claude identity or an invented endpoint. Keep all dependencies/settings explicit.

This task and Claude have separate provider ownership; parallel future writers still require disjoint owned worktrees. Fixture and native evidence remain distinct, while unsupported controls, unknown metadata, cessation and settlement use the common kernel contracts.
